Aim: To determine whether metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers improve identification of screen-detected high blood pressure among US adults without previously reported hypertension.
Data: NHANES 2017–2018.
Population: Adults aged 20 years or older without previously reported hypertension and with valid blood-pressure measurements.
Primary outcome: Screen-detected high blood pressure, defined as mean systolic blood pressure over 140 mmHg or mean diastolic blood pressure over 90 mmHg.
Primary comparison: A baseline model containing age, sex and BMI versus a biomarker-augmented model additionally containing HbA1c, HDL cholesterol and hs-CRP.
Machine-learning comparison: Random forest using the same predictors as the biomarker-augmented statistical model.
Evaluation: Discrimination, calibration, classification performance and exploratory subgroup performance.
Sensitivity analysis: Alternative blood-pressure threshold of over 130/80 mmHg for systolic and diastolic blood pressure respectively.
Interpretation: This cross-sectional analysis evaluates identification rather than future cardiovascular risk prediction and cannot establish causal relationships.
